basics.name: Obed Junias
basics.label: Computer Science Graduate Student & NLP Researcher
basics.summary: I am a graduate researcher exploring Commonsense Reasoning, Neuro-symbolic NLP, and Responsible ML. My research focuses on developing reasoning frameworks that integrate structured logic with neural representations, with the goal of improving the interpretability, factual consistency, and fairness of LLMs. I aspire to contribute to foundational AI research at the intersection of cognition, reasoning, and ethical deployment.

research.organization: Institute of Cognitive Science, CU Boulder
research.summary: Conducting fairness and bias evaluations of large language models (LLaMA, GPT-4, etc.) in mental health classification tasks, analyzing demographic and modality-based disparities in model behavior.
highlights: Implemented fairness-aware loss functions and diagnostic probes for LLM evaluation
Identified demographic and linguistic biases in model outputs across text and audio modalities
Co-author of an accepted IEEE-EMBS 2025 paper (arXiv:2509.25795) on algorithmic bias in mental health detection
Developing frameworks for ethical and responsible AI deployment

research.position: Graduate Researcher – Medical Ethics and NLP
research.summary: Examining the ethical and commonsense reasoning capabilities of LLMs in clinical and biomedical contexts using controlled evaluation pipelines.
highlights: Developed the Medical Ethics Assessment of LLMs project using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline
Analyzed model confidence and rationale structures to assess reliability in moral reasoning tasks
Identified key gaps in ethical reasoning consistency even under knowledge-augmented setups
Contributing to responsible NLP research focused on model interpretability and societal alignment

projects.name: Medical Ethics Assessment of LLMs
projects.summary: Systematic assessment of ethical reasoning capabilities of large language models in clinical contexts using RAG pipeline and controlled evaluation with curated multiple-choice questions.

projects.name: Lost in Plot: Contrastive Learning for Movie Retrieval
projects.summary: Dense retrieval system using fine-tuned BERT encoder with contrastive learning for tip-of-the-tongue movie retrieval, outperforming GPT-4 baseline on 100K+ movie corpus.

projects.name: Resource-Efficient LLM Fine-tuning for Mental Health Support
projects.summary: Applied parameter-efficient fine-tuning with QLoRA to adapt Falcon 7B model for mental health conversations with limited computational resources.

projects.name: Multi-stage RAG System
projects.summary: Robust RAG system with FAISS indexing and Scikit-Learn context filtering for enhanced factual grounding of LLM responses over research paper corpus.
